The STATdx rendering is selected for default download so the full STATdx image set remains contiguous; the RadPrimer rendering is archive-optional for traceability/recovery. === DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS === - [RadPrimer] Common: Focal nodular hyperplasia; hepatic cavernous hemangioma. - [RadPrimer] Less common: Hepatocellular carcinoma; hepatic adenoma; hepatic metastases; fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma; intrahepatic/peripheral cholangiocarcinoma; epithelioid hemangioendothelioma. - [RadPrimer] Rare but important: Nodular regenerative hyperplasia, especially large regenerative nodules in Budd-Chiari syndrome. === HIGH-YIELD DISCRIMINATORS === - [Both] Start with scar size, scar calcification, enhancement pattern of the mass/scar, multiplicity, and associated findings such as vascular invasion, biliary obstruction, capsular retraction, or Budd-Chiari morphology. - [Both] FNH and cholangiocarcinoma are usually solitary, fibrolamellar carcinoma is almost always solitary, and hemangiomas, metastases, epithelioid hemangioendothelioma, HCC, and nodular regenerative hyperplasia may be multiple depending on clinical setting. - [Both] Calcified scar strongly favors fibrolamellar HCC or giant hemangioma. Calcification is uncommon/rare in FNH, conventional HCC, adenoma, cholangiocarcinoma, and most metastases, but mucinous metastases such as colon/ovarian cancer can calcify. - [Both] A true scar should be separated from necrosis, hemorrhage, fibrosis, fat, or treated tumor. Adenoma and metastases often mimic scar because of hemorrhage, necrosis, fat, or fibrosis rather than a true central scar. === DIAGNOSIS-SPECIFIC SYNTHESIS === - [Both] Focal nodular hyperplasia: Larger lesions often have a small central scar and thin radiating septa. The mass enhances homogeneously in the arterial phase and becomes isoattenuating/isointense to liver on later phases. The scar is bright on T2, may show delayed enhancement with CT or intravascular MR agents, and does not enhance/retain gadoxetate on delayed hepatobiliary imaging. Use STATdx images 1-3 as the primary FNH teaching cluster. - [Both] Hepatic cavernous hemangioma: Large or giant hemangiomas may have a fibrotic nonenhancing central scar that may calcify, while nonscar tissue shows peripheral nodular discontinuous enhancement with progressive fill-in. Very bright T2 signal supports hemangioma. Use STATdx images 4-6 as the primary hemangioma cluster. - [Both] Conventional hepatocellular carcinoma: Large tumors, especially in a noncirrhotic liver, can resemble fibrolamellar HCC because they are heterogeneous, hypervascular, and may have washout with central necrosis or scar. Scar calcification is rare in conventional HCC. Vascular invasion and metastatic disease support HCC. Use STATdx images 7-8 for mosaic enhancement, necrosis/scar, and portal vein tumor invasion. - [Both] Hepatic adenoma: Low-density or low-signal regions usually represent fat, necrosis, or old hemorrhage rather than a true scar. Chemical-shift MRI can show signal drop from fat. Calcification is uncommon. Eovist-enhanced MRI is most useful for distinction from FNH. Use STATdx images 9-10 as adenoma-pattern reinforcement for hemorrhage/necrosis/fibrosis and nonenhancing central abnormality. - [Both] Hepatic metastases: Target appearance and central low density usually reflect necrosis or fibrosis rather than a true scar. Fibrous stroma may be prominent after treatment or in some primaries. Calcification is uncommon overall but can be seen with mucinous metastases such as colon or ovarian cancer. Use STATdx images 11-12 together as the colon-cancer metastasis cluster. - [Both] Fibrolamellar HCC: Classically a large heterogeneous mass in a young patient, often with a large central scar that is calcified in more than half of cases. Aggressive features such as local vascular/biliary invasion and metastases are common at presentation. Use STATdx images 13-15 as the fibrolamellar cluster, including nodal disease and calcified scar. - [Both] Intrahepatic/peripheral cholangiocarcinoma: Focal necrosis or fibrosis can mimic scar. Extensive fibrous stroma produces progressive delayed enhancement. Capsular retraction, hepatic volume loss, biliary obstruction, and portal venous obstruction are key supporting clues. Use STATdx images 16-17 as the CT/MR cholangiocarcinoma cluster. - [Both] Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma: Usually multiple peripheral nodules that may coalesce. Target or lollipop appearance and capsular retraction are important clues. Use STATdx images 18-19 for target/capsular retraction and T2 central necrosis or scar. - [Both] Nodular regenerative hyperplasia / large regenerative nodules: Multiacinar large regenerative nodules can have central scars, are usually multiple and less than 4 cm, and are classically associated with Budd-Chiari syndrome. Hepatobiliary agent retention supports functional hepatocytes with deficient biliary ducts. Use STATdx images 20-24 as the Budd-Chiari/NRH imaging-pathology cluster, including trichrome confirmation. === SELECTED PRIMARY IMAGE SET === - STATdx image 1: Axial arterial-phase CECT shows a homogeneously and brightly enhancing mass with a central scar . The mass became isodense with liver on portal venous phase. Used for: focalNodularHyperplasia, arterialHyperenhancement, centralScar, recognitionReinforcement, axialArterialCECT. - STATdx image 2: Axial 20-minute delayed T1 MR shows a large mass that retains contrast more than underlying liver. The central scar does not take up or retain gadoxetate. Used for: focalNodularHyperplasia, hepatobiliaryContrast, gadoxetateScarNonretention, recognitionReinforcement, delayedT1MR. - STATdx image 3: Axial T1 C+ FS MR shows a brightly and homogeneously enhancing mass with a central scar ; this is classic FNH. Used for: focalNodularHyperplasia, classicHomogeneousEnhancement, centralScar, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement, axialT1PostContrastMR. - STATdx image 4: Axial CECT shows a large mass with peripheral nodular enhancement isodense to vessels. A central scar , with a small focus of calcification, did not fill in on delayed imaging. These are typical features of giant hemangiomas. Used for: giantHemangioma, peripheralNodularEnhancement, calcifiedCentralScar, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 5: Axial T2 MR shows a large, hyperintense mass with a central scar that is very bright, typical of a large hemangioma with progressive nodular enhancement on arterial , venous , and delayed phases. Used for: giantHemangioma, veryBrightT2Scar, multiphasicProgressiveEnhancement, atomicMultipanelCluster, recognitionReinforcement, axialT2MR. - STATdx image 6: Axial T2 MR shows a large mass that is very bright and well defined. A central scar is even more intense, typical of large cavernous hemangioma. Used for: cavernousHemangioma, veryBrightT2Mass, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement, axialT2MR. - STATdx image 7: Axial arterial-phase CECT in an older woman shows a large, heterogeneous, hypervascular mass with foci of necrosis, giving it a mottled or mosaic appearance. The age of the patient and absence of calcification favored conventional hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), as opposed to fibrolamellar HCC, confirmed on biopsy. Used for: conventionalHCC, mosaicMottledEnhancement, necrosis, olderPatient, recognitionReinforcement, axialArterialCECT. - STATdx image 8: Axial CECT shows a large mass with an eccentric scar or necrotic area. Tumor invasion of portal vein helps to identify this as HCC. Used for: hepatocellularCarcinoma, eccentricScarOrNecrosis, portalVeinTumorInvasion, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 9: Axial NECT shows a heterogeneous mass in the left lobe. At resection, the focus of high attenuation was hemorrhage, and the lower density foci were necrosis and fibrosis. Used for: hepaticAdenomaPattern, hemorrhageNecrosisFibrosis, leftLobeMass, recognitionReinforcement, axialNECT. - STATdx image 10: Axial venous-phase T1 C+ MR shows a large, enhancing mass with a central nonenhancing scar . Used for: hepaticAdenomaPattern, enhancingMassWithNonenhancingScar, MRVariant, recognitionReinforcement, venousPhaseT1PostContrastMR. - STATdx image 11: Axial NECT in this older patient with colon cancer shows shows multiple lesions with faint central calcification . Used for: mucinousColonMetastases, centralCalcification, noncontrastDetection, samePatientCluster, recognitionReinforcement, axialNECT. - STATdx image 12: Axial portal venous-phase CECT in this older patient with colon cancer shows multiple metastases with central, low-density necrosis or fibrosis. The faint calcification is more difficult to recognize on contrast-enhanced imaging. Used for: mucinousColonMetastases, centralNecrosisOrFibrosis, contrastPhaseComparison, samePatientCluster, recognitionReinforcement, portalVenousCECT. - STATdx image 13: Axial CECT in a 22-year-old man shows a heterogeneous, hypervascular mass with a large, calcified central scar . Note the similar enhancement of tumor in a cardiophrenic node . Used for: fibrolamellarHCC, calcifiedCentralScar, hypervascularTumor, cardiophrenicNodeMetastasis, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 14: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in a young woman with a large, heterogeneously enhancing left hepatic lobe fibrolamellar HCC shows a central necrotic scar . Used for: fibrolamellarHCC, necroticCentralScar, youngWoman, MRVariant, recognitionReinforcement, T1PostContrastFSMR. - STATdx image 15: Axial CECT shows a large mass that fills the left lobe with low density and calcified portions of the scar. Used for: fibrolamellarHCC, calcifiedScar, largeLeftLobeMass, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 16: Axial CECT shows a large hepatic mass with foci of scar or necrosis . Capsular retraction and occlusion of the portal vein and bile duct help confirm cholangiocarcinoma. Used for: cholangiocarcinoma, capsularRetraction, portalVeinOcclusion, bileDuctOcclusion, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 17: Axial T1 C+ FS MR shows a large, hypointense mass with progressive enhancement on arterial , portal venous , and delayed phases due to fibrotic changes and a nonenhancing central scar . Used for: cholangiocarcinoma, progressiveFibroticEnhancement, nonenhancingCentralScar, atomicMultipanelCluster, recognitionReinforcement, T1PostContrastFSMR. - STATdx image 18: Axial CECT in a young woman shows multiple peripheral hypovascular lesions with a target appearance. The subcapsular lesions are associated with retraction of the overlying liver capsule . Used for: epithelioidHemangioendothelioma, targetAppearance, subcapsularCapsularRetraction, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 19: Axial T2 FS MR in a young woman shows multiple peripheral and confluent masses , many with hyperintense central necrosis or scar . These are typical features of hepatic epithelial hemangioendothelioma. Used for: epithelioidHemangioendothelioma, multifocalPeripheralConfluentMasses, T2CentralNecrosisOrScar, recognitionReinforcement, T2FSMR. - STATdx image 20: Axial arterial-phase T1 C+ MR in a hypercoagulable patient shows multiple hypervascular foci . Some of the lesions seem to have a hypointense rim, while others have a hypointense central scar . Used for: nodularRegenerativeHyperplasia, BuddChiari, hypervascularNodules, centralScar, samePatientCluster, recognitionReinforcement, arterialT1PostContrastMR. - STATdx image 21: Axial T1 C+ MR in a hypercoagulable patient 2 hours after IV administration of gadobenate dimeglumine shows persistent uptake and retention of the agent within the nodules , indicating functional hepatocytes and deficient biliary ducts within the lesions. Used for: nodularRegenerativeHyperplasia, BuddChiari, hepatobiliaryAgentRetention, functionalHepatocytes, samePatientCluster, recognitionReinforcement, delayedT1PostContrastMR. - STATdx image 22: Axial T1 C+ MR in a patient with Budd-Chiari syndrome shows multiple hypervascular nodules , some of which have a central scar . These multiple large, regenerative nodules (nodular regenerative hyperplasia) confirmed transplantation. Used for: nodularRegenerativeHyperplasia, BuddChiari, multipleLargeRegenerativeNodules, transplantConfirmation, recognitionReinforcement, T1PostContrastMR. - STATdx image 23: Axial CECT in a patient with Budd-Chiari syndrome and nodular regenerative hyperplasia shows a central scar and doughnut-like enhancement. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is also seen . Used for: nodularRegenerativeHyperplasia, BuddChiari, doughnutEnhancement, TIPSContext, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 24: In this patient with Budd-Chiari syndrome and multiple hypervascular nodules, trichrome stain shows green staining of the central scar and the capsule of the nodule, typical features of the macroscopic form of nodular regenerative hyperplasia or large regenerative nodules. Used for: nodularRegenerativeHyperplasia, BuddChiari, histologyCorrelation, trichromeCentralScar, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement. === ARCHIVE-OPTIONAL DUPLICATE IMAGES === - RadPrimer image 1: archiveOptionalDuplicate.
